clue.text: Casualty royal forces couldn't help after shell burst

definitions.text: Casualty royal forces couldn't help after shell burst

parts.words: Casualty royal forces couldn't help after shell burst
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme egg who fell off a wall: all the king's horses and men could not mend his broken shell

explanation.surface: A war report of a soldier beyond the help of the army after an artillery shell exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell burst' suggests artillery, but it is an eggshell cracking; the 'royal forces' are the king's horses and men of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's egg-shaped character falls, breaks and cannot be put together again, making him the archetypal casualty.

clue.text: In German city, ring for a hat

indicators.note: ring for a means one letter is swapped in place of the other in the city name

parts.note: Hamburg is a port city in Germany
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone in a German city exchanging a ring for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the A in HAMBURG to O.
explanation.definitionFit: A homburg is a felt hat with a dented crown and curled brim, named after a German spa town.

clue.text: Artistic old lady making a profit, so to speak

explanation.surface: An elderly woman artist who is doing well financially.
explanation.walkthrough: Grandma Moses was an American folk painter who began in old age; 'profit, so to speak' plays on prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandma Moses painted late in life; the biblical Moses was a prophet, which sounds like profit.

clue.text: Traffic sign's distinctive feature

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, buy and sell
a mark is a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: A road sign's distinctive look.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic feature by which a person or thing is recognised is figuratively their signature mark.

clue.text: Appreciates accommodation

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: To dig something is slang for liking it; digs is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'dig' means like or understand; British 'digs' are rented rooms or lodgings.

clue.text: Find similar wood for a small container

parts.note: to match is to find something similar or equal
box is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Seeking matching timber to make a small box.
explanation.definitionFit: The small cardboard case holding matchsticks is a little container.

clue.text: Leave after using last of that fabric

indicators.note: after puts the word for leave behind the letter
last of picks the final letter of the word that

parts.note: to leave something in a will is to bequeath it, so will means leave

explanation.surface: Someone told to go after finishing up that fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: T (the last letter of 'that') is followed by WILL; 'Leave' is the verb bequeath, not depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a woven cloth with diagonal ribs, such as denim or gabardine.

clue.text: Drawing instruments — likely to be rulers?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a set of drawing tools includes rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dividers are a compass-like tool for measuring; 'divide and rule' makes dividers those likely to govern.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividers are a two-pointed measuring tool; by the maxim divide and rule, those who divide are the ones who govern.

clue.text: It inspires pity in quiet Dumas hero

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Athos is one of the Three Musketeers in Alexandre Dumas's novel

explanation.surface: A musketeer whose quiet manner makes people feel sorry for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that moves people to sorrow or compassion.

clue.text: Poorly instructed girl fully stretched, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a girl is a miss, and fully stretched is taut, giving miss taut

explanation.surface: A badly trained young woman pulled tight.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS TAUT spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mistaught is to have been taught wrongly or badly.

clue.text: Island's business restricted by return of capital

indicators.note: restricted by means the business word is held within the other letters
return of means the letters for capital are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, capital; read as letters AI
biz is informal shorthand for business

explanation.surface: An island's commerce limited by capital flowing back out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns AI (A1, first-rate) into IA; 'restricted by' sets the business word inside it. 'Capital' looks like a city but means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish Mediterranean isle in the Balearics; 's stands for 'is' joining definition to wordplay.

clue.text: Cover for man in politically sensitive area

explanation.surface: Protection for someone in a troubled region.
explanation.walkthrough: An ulster is a long loose overcoat; Ulster is Northern Ireland, long politically contested.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long men's overcoat; the province of Northern Ireland has been the scene of political conflict.

clue.text: Juvenile with kite, a pretty girl

parts.note: chil (or cheel) is an Indian name for the kite bird
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A youngster flying a kite with a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kite' is the bird of prey, not a toy; CHIL is its Hindi name.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish and juvenile both describe immature behaviour suited to a young person.

clue.text: Contracted a poor actor in place of fools, apparently

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it, so contracted means got
a ham is an overacting, poor actor

explanation.surface: Hiring a bad actor for a village of simpletons.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is the English village whose 'wise men' feigned folly; 'apparently' admits their foolishness was an act.
explanation.definitionFit: The villagers of the Nottinghamshire village were proverbially fools, as told in the Wise Men tales.

clue.text: Article about one jolly sort of roguish activity

indicators.note: about means the article goes round the letter for one

parts.note: the is the definite article
one is the Roman numeral I
jolly is British informal for very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a cheerful kind of rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the article round the letter for one; 'jolly' is British informal for very, not cheerful. 'sort of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the activity of rogues and thieves.

clue.text: Refreshing drinks for workers at last? Nonsense!

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing at cool drinks for workers at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: a cobbler is an iced drink; cobblers mend shoes on a last (a foot-shaped block); 'cobblers' is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers are iced wine cocktails, shoe-menders using a last, and British slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Inspiration could make one view a barn differently

indicators.note: differently says the letters of the words are arranged in another order

explanation.surface: A sudden idea that would let you see a farm building in a new light.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever idea, a flash of insight.

clue.text: Grey mare's last rider, for one, was a slave

definitions.text: Grey mare's last rider, for one

explanation.surface: The final rider of an old grey horse once lived in bondage.
explanation.walkthrough: In the folk song Widecombe Fair, Uncle Tom Cobley is the last named of those riding Tom Pearce's grey mare; Uncle Tom is the enslaved hero of Uncle Tom's Cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Tom Cobley ends the list of riders in the Devon song; the title character of Stowe's novel was enslaved.

clue.text: Louis VI certainly wasn't contemplative

explanation.surface: A remark that a French king was no deep thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Louis VI of France was called Louis the Fat, so he was not a THIN KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis VI was known as the Fat, the opposite of a slender monarch; a pensive person is deep in thought.

clue.text: Informed about steel centre, old city in Spain

indicators.note: about means informed wraps round the centre of steel

parts.note: informed means told

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letter of the word steel

explanation.surface: Being told about a steel-making city in old Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo really was famed for steel blades, which disguises 'steel centre' as a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic walled city in central Spain, once the capital.

clue.text: Bones found in Turkish city

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains discovered in a city in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsus is the set of ankle bones; Tarsus is the Turkish city, birthplace of St Paul.

clue.text: Extend in time

explanation.surface: An instruction to lengthen something within a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' here is a prison sentence: a stretch is a spell inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch is to lengthen; a stretch is slang for a prison term.

clue.text: Be followed by flower-girl in brisk fashion

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
Lily is a girl's name that is also a flower

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid with flowers following behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Livelily is an adverb meaning energetically, with spirit.

clue.text: The dignified part of popular government

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark on the stately aspect of democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a slow, stately and broad movement; the noun phrase names that grave quality.

clue.text: Not just ugly?

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is not merely ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely' but means fair-minded; 'fair' also means pretty, so not fair is ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking justice is unjust; if fair means beautiful, its negation suggests plain-looking.

clue.text: Something that might save face, we hear, could be an advantage

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase counts by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a veil covers and shields the face, so a veil is something that might save it

explanation.surface: A face-saving gesture could prove beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save face' suggests avoiding embarrassment, but it means protect the face, as a veil does.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Look around St Paul's for his monument

definitions.text: Look around St Paul's for his monument

parts.words: Look around St Paul's for his monument
parts.note: the Latin epitaph in St Paul's Cathedral for its architect says if you seek his monument, look around

explanation.surface: A visitor told to survey a London cathedral to find a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: The epitaph 'si monumentum requiris, circumspice' in St Paul's honours the architect who designed the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral, so the building itself is his memorial.

clue.text: He made engravings of French king and queen

parts.note: du is French for of the
r is short for rex, Latin for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An artist who engraved portraits of a French royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French king' tempts ROI, but 'of French' is DU and king is R.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was the German Renaissance master of woodcut and engraving.

clue.text: Name a dreadful nag? Exactly!

parts.note: a term is a name or word for something

indicators.note: dreadful means the letters of the word nag are badly jumbled

parts.note: to a T means exactly, giving T

explanation.surface: Someone asking for the name of an awful scold and being told they have it right.
explanation.walkthrough: GAN comes from rearranging NAG; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, overbearing, scolding woman, a shrew.

clue.text: State's popular reform of the law

parts.note: common means of the people, popular

indicators.note: reform of means the words the law are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A nation is pressing for a popular rewrite of its legal code.
explanation.walkthrough: WEALTH is the rearranged THE LAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonwealth is a political community or nation, such as Massachusetts or Australia.
